title: LLM Agents for Interactive Workflow Provenance: Reference Architecture and Evaluation Methodology
problem: Large-scale workflow provenance data becomes complex and difficult to analyze at scale; existing query approaches (custom scripts, structured queries, dashboards) limit interactivity
motivation: Scientific discovery workflows span Edge/Cloud/HPC; comprehensive data analysis essential for reproducibility and hypothesis validation; natural language querying could improve accessibility
method: LLM agent-based interactive provenance analysis; metadata-driven design translating NL to structured provenance queries; RAG and prompt tuning; evaluation on LLaMA, GPT, Gemini, Claude across diverse query classes
key_novelty: LLM agents for interactive provenance query and analysis; RAG-enabled natural language interface to workflow metadata
contributions: Reference architecture for LLM-based provenance analysis
Evaluation methodology for LLM agent effectiveness
Open-source implementation of LLM agent interface
Validation across multiple LLM providers and real workflow
limitations: Evaluation limited to one real workflow; generalization to other workflow types uncertain
primary_theme: Interactive workflow analysis via LLM agents
